summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with advanced HIV, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of herpes zoster with post-herpetic neuralgia was admitted after developing sudden lightheadedness, weakness, and nausea following a dialysis session. Initially, sepsis was suspected due to her immunocompromised state, and she received IV fluids and empiric antibiotics. However, her symptoms were attributed to a side effect of pregabalin (Lyrica), which she had started two days prior and had previously reacted to with gabapentin. Blood cultures showed no growth, antibiotics were discontinued, and Lyrica was stopped. Her symptoms improved, and she was transitioned to duloxetine for neuropathic pain, dosed appropriately for renal failure. Medication reconciliation revealed gaps in HIV treatment adherence, and plans were made to restart antiretroviral therapy with outpatient support. She was discharged home with services, with follow-up arranged for HIV, mental health, and medication management.
